title: Delivery journey case definition
description: One delivery journey case. The case DECLARES the scenario identity, the module/actions that realize it and the evidence it must leave; tools/verify/delivery-journey.mjs only adapts and executes what is declared (spawn real commands, read real state, collect evidence) and emits a structured verdict. Division of labor (verification_runner_invariant): the runner is a test action/observer adapter, NOT a controller — it owns no phase, no DAG, no retries, no job lease and no auto-recovery; those semantics live in the case definition and the upstream contract (execution-contract.json). Verdict semantics: PASS = actions executed (execution count > 0) and every expected outcome met; FAIL = the scenario executed and the observed outcome contradicted the frozen THEN; NOT-EXERCISED = a prerequisite was missing (case definition, registered baseline, identity or environment) — structured refusal with nonzero exit, never converted into a pass; NOT-APPLICABLE = the scenario is explicitly out of scope for the registered profile with a recorded reason (still nonzero; the runner never self-assigns it).

schemaVersion.description: Definition format version; mismatches are refused, never coerced.

scenario.description: Stable scenario id (e.g. A01, B07, M02) matching the verification-case-plan key and the frozen spec scenario heading.

acceptanceIds.description: Acceptance ids this case provides execution evidence for.

caseModule.description: Case module that realizes the scenario (absolute, or repo-relative like test/delivery-cases/2_1.mjs). The canonical plan-driven action is `node --test <caseModule>`.

path.description: Frozen spec file holding the scenario definition.

requirement.description: Requirement heading the scenario belongs to.

type.description: spawn = run a real command; readState = read a real file (relative paths resolve against the evidence dir); inspect = record a read-only observation (a command like 'git rev-parse HEAD' or a filesystem path).

command.description: Required for spawn: the exact argv line to execute (whitespace-split; no shell).

path.description: Required for readState/inspect: file path or observation spec.

expected.description: Human-auditable expected outcome; recorded in the verdict next to the actual outcome.

artifacts.description: Evidence artifacts the journey must leave in --evidence-dir (e.g. case-definition.json, action-1-stdout.txt, verdict.json). A missing artifact is a journey failure: a claim without persisted bytes is not evidence.
